Enabled by default.name: Host and screenshot restrictions for chrome.debugger API
Enabled by default.summary:
### Update (November 4, 2026): Feature rollback

Based on customer feedback, the enforcement of an all-or-nothing enterprise policy for the [`chrome.debugger` extension API](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/extensions/reference/api/debugger) can cause issues in certain environments. 

While we design a more flexible approach, we have decided to roll back this change. For details on how to apply the rollback, see our addendum to this [Chrome Developer blog post](https://developer.chrome.com/blog/debugger-enterprise-policy-restrictions#guidance_for_enterprise_administrators).

### Feature description (September 23, 2026)

The [`chrome.debugger` extension API](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/extensions/reference/api/debugger) lets you send [Chrome DevTools Protocol](https://chromedevtools.github.io/devtools-protocol/) commands to a specified `target`, for example, a tab, an iframe, or a service worker. When connecting (attaching) to a target, the API can now enforce permissions on managed browsers by validating enterprise host and screenshot policies.

On enterprise devices, some policies can restrict extensions from attaching the debugger using an all-or-nothing model at attach time (`chrome.debugger.attach()`):

- For hosts, the [ExtensionSettings](https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#ExtensionSettings) enterprise policy can be configured to block hosts for an extension, returning the error `Host access is restricted by policy`.
- For screenshots, the [DisableScreenshots](https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#DisableScreenshots) enterprise policy disables screenshot capture or Data Loss Prevention (DLP) rules apply, returning the error `Screenshot capture is restricted by policy`.

Developers can handle attach rejections gracefully or use higher-level APIs like [`chrome.scripting`](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/extensions/reference/api/scripting) and [`chrome.declarativeNetRequest`](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/extensions/reference/api/declarativeNetRequest) that support granular origin permissions in restricted enterprise environments.
Enabled by default.creator: sadym@google.com

Enabled by default.name: Margin-trim
Enabled by default.summary:
The `margin-trim` CSS property may be used to omit margins before or after the first or last child of a container. This is supported on regular block containers and multicol containers.

This is somewhat similar to the effect caused by the margin quirk that is applied to P, H1, H2... elements inside BODY and table cell elements (in quirks mode), but more powerful, generic, and expressive.

Note: A previous version of the spec also applied this for flex and grid containers, but this has been removed.
Enabled by default.creator: mstensho@chromium.org

Enabled by default.name: Pause media playback on not-visible iframes
Enabled by default.summary: Adds a "media-playback-while-not-visible" permission policy to allow embedders to pause audible media playback of embedded iframes which are currently hidden - i.e. "display" property set to "none"; "visibility" property set to "hidden"; or zero-area (width or height equal to 0). While hidden, attempts made by the embedded iframe to render audible media will be blocked. When the frame is shown again the prohibitions should be lifted. This should allow developers to build more user-friendly experiences and to also improve the performance by letting the browser handle the playback of content that is not visible to users.
Enabled by default.creator: gabrielbrito@microsoft.com

maturity.text: Specification being incubated in a Community Group

view.notes:
The community is supportive of resolving this problem using a permission policy. A commenter mentioned that the proposal fits well within the Permissions Policy API specification. They also agree that there is no workaround for this problem using current web API's. 

Feedback has been addressed to also include other invisibility scenarios like zero-area (height or width equal to 0) and to change the API name from "not-rendered" to "not-visible".

Enabled by default.name: Server Side Gemini Powered Scam Checks for Desktop
Enabled by default.summary: We are expanding server side Gemini powered scam checks from just Android to desktop as well. This replaces the desktop on device model powered checks previously used.These checks are only for users enrolled in Enhanced Safe Browsing. Enterprises can control enrollment for their organization through the existing SafeBrowsingProtectionLevel policy. Chrome minimizes the amount of data shared with the server by only analyzing page text when a site exhibits high-confidence scam indicators. And whenever page content is sent off the device, it is processed ephemerally – meaning it is never logged, retained or used to train models.

In developer trial (Behind a flag).name: WebTransport Datagram writable streams and prioritization
In developer trial (Behind a flag).summary:
Adds the modern WebTransport Datagram sending API.

WebTransportDatagramDuplexStream.createWritable() creates independent WebTransportDatagramsWritable streams. Each writable has mutable sendGroup and sendOrder attributes for expressing relative priority among queued WebTransport data in the same send group. Chromium currently applies this ordering among Datagram writables.

The implementation also reports the negotiated maximum outgoing Datagram payload size and discards oversized writes as required by the WebTransport specification.
In developer trial (Behind a flag).creator: monicach@microsoft.com

In developer trial (Behind a flag).name: WebTransport reliability attributes
In developer trial (Behind a flag).summary:
Adds the WebTransport.reliability instance attribute and static WebTransport.supportsReliableOnly attribute. These APIs indicate whether the user agent supports WebTransport over exclusively reliable connections and whether an established session supports unreliable transport such as datagrams.

In Chromium, reliability initially returns "pending" and changes to "supports-unreliable" after an HTTP/3 WebTransport connection is established.  Since Chromium does not currently support HTTP/2 fallback,  WebTransport.supportsReliableOnly returns false; any successfully established session uses HTTP/3 and supports unreliable datagrams.
In developer trial (Behind a flag).creator: monicach@microsoft.com
